reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-level context, the full `ImmunizationEvaluation` StructureDefinition report, direct behavior findings whose `affectedResources` include `ImmunizationEvaluation`, representative shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context, the deterministic aggregate only after forming the resource judgment, and local R4/R6 package evidence for the resource identity and candidate Immunization fields.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `ImmunizationEvaluation` is FMM 0/trial-use, so the stability burden is weak and resource retirement is more plausible than it would be for mature or normative content. That weak pressure does not erase the clinical/public-health relevance of dose-validity determinations or the value of preserving a low-friction migration path.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 removal of the `ImmunizationEvaluation` resource makes a migration program unavoidable, but preserving a transition identity, successor mapping, and dose-validity semantics still has material value.

reasoning.thesisMd: `ImmunizationEvaluation` is not a mostly stable resource with a few changed elements. R4 defines a concrete resource for evaluating whether an immunization event counted toward recommendations, while the supplied R6 ballot package has no same-name StructureDefinition or index entry. Existing R4 instances therefore cannot validate or route as R6 resources without a resource-level conversion decision. The resource's low FMM softens the compatibility burden, but the subject matter is safety/public-health relevant enough that the removal and lack of a standard successor should not be treated as mere cleanup.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The dominant migration shape is resource retirement or replacement. Implementers must identify all R4 `ImmunizationEvaluation` records, choose a target representation, preserve links to the evaluated `Immunization`, patient, target disease, authority, series and dose numbering where needed, and decide how to carry the core evaluation outcome. R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` overlaps with some protocol metadata, but its definition is about the protocol followed by the administering provider, not a retrospective dose-validity evaluation.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The resource-identity break means a broad migration program is already unavoidable as the R6 package currently stands; preserving individual old element names inside the removed resource would not by itself solve interoperability. However, that does not mean additional compatibility preservation is valueless. A deprecated/transition resource identity, an explicit base successor/backbone, retained terminology, or documented endpoint/search aliases where semantics are one-to-one could reduce silent data loss and implementation-specific divergence. For that reason the practical posture is to preserve compatibility where it is low-cost while still expecting a resource migration.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest less-breaking option is to retain `ImmunizationEvaluation` in R6 as deprecated or transition-only while pointing new implementations to the intended successor pattern. If that is too costly, the next best base-compatible approach is an explicit standard R6 carrier or profile for evaluation outcomes plus normative conversion guidance for `doseStatus` and `doseStatusReason`. Keeping only local extensions or private ConceptMaps is useful mitigation but does not provide the same cross-implementation compatibility.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The two direct behavior findings are in scope and reinforce the same resource-removal story: the base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises an `ImmunizationEvaluation` REST surface, and search parameters whose only base was the removed resource disappear. These are real client/server migration issues, but they are derivative of the resource lifecycle decision rather than independent reasons to reclassify the migration shape. The 11 shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings were treated as context only because this review is for `ImmunizationEvaluation`, not the base resource types.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that major migration is already unavoidable and that the migration shape is `removed-or-replaced-resource`. I differ on compatibility leverage: the aggregate selected `migration-program-dominates`, while this review uses `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration` because all three structure findings point to plausible preservation or transition mechanisms, and the dose-validity semantics are central enough that avoiding avoidable data loss remains valuable despite FMM 0.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high that the R6 ballot package lacks the resource and that the behavior surface disappears with it. Confidence is lower about HL7's intended replacement because the local inputs do not include official ballot rationale, narrative migration guidance, or an authoritative cross-version mapping.

findingConsiderations.title: ImmunizationEvaluation resource is absent from the R6 core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the resource-level hard break. An R4 instance with `resourceType: ImmunizationEvaluation` has no supplied R6 core definition, generated model, resource enum, or normal REST route. It makes migration unavoidable and is the main standards-review-worthy decision.

findingConsiderations.title: No lossless standard R6 mapping target is evident for the evaluation record
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This finding determines whether the resource retirement is merely mechanical or requires policy judgment. Because no evident R6 target preserves the evaluation result as a first-class fact, migration can be lossy and implementation-specific unless standards guidance supplies a successor or conversion rule.

findingConsiderations.title: Dose-validity status and reason terminology are no longer first-class fields on a standard R6 resource
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not an independent hard validation break because the whole resource is already absent and the R4 bindings were example strength. It still matters because `doseStatus` is mandatory in R4 and carries the clinically important valid/not-valid outcome used by forecasting, audit, and public-health workflows.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For `ImmunizationEvaluation`, this is the REST/API manifestation of the resource removal. It is relevant to generated route inventories and conformance tests, but the endpoint question should be resolved through the resource retirement or transition design rather than treated as a separate model break.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Queries against the old `ImmunizationEvaluation` endpoint and its resource-specific search surface have no same-base R6 target. This adds real client migration work, but it is derivative of the missing resource and should be addressed by explicit endpoint/search migration guidance or aliases only where the successor semantics are clear.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared `Resource` operation change may affect clients that operate generically on many resource types, but it is not specific to `ImmunizationEvaluation` and was not scored as part of the resource-level migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` search metadata change is relevant background for generic clients, but it does not alter the conclusion that `ImmunizationEvaluation`'s dominant break is resource removal.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Ask the responsible work group to document or revisit the retirement decision: either keep `ImmunizationEvaluation` as a deprecated/transition resource for R6, or publish an explicit standard R6 successor and conversion map that preserves the evaluated immunization, target disease, dose-validity result, reasons, and series context.

If the resource remains retired, define a standard way to carry `doseStatus` and `doseStatusReason` semantics, including the valid/not-valid outcome and reason-code mapping, so public-health and forecasting implementations do not invent incompatible extensions.

Document REST and search migration expectations for the removed endpoint. Consider transition endpoint/search aliases only when there is a clear one-to-one successor; otherwise state the incompatibility and required data-model conversion explicitly.

caveats: The review is based on the local R4 package, R6 ballot4 package, generated reports, and behavior reports; no official ballot disposition or narrative migration guide was available locally.
R4 FMM 0/trial-use weakens the compatibility expectation and makes resource retirement more acceptable than for mature resources.
The review treats shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior findings as context only, per the resource-review instructions.
